title: The tailpipe cover
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover is the Datsun's tailpipe with the uncle's clamp on it, close, and one clean puff. The owner says it's a pipe. Wood says it's the first thing he's fixed. She says he didn't fix it. He says he held the can.

panels.composition: The cover: a tailpipe, a clamp, gravel, one clean puff of exhaust. Close.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing a car's tailpipe with a clamp on it above gravel and one clean puff of exhaust, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner. WOOD. BARNABY, still faintly wavy.

balloons.text: It's the first thing I've fixed.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet while a young man and a faintly smelly small dog wait, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The owner, sniffing. Looking at the dog.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner sniffing and looking down at a small dog with suspicion, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack. The pipe on the cover. The dog banished to the doorway by a look. The strip has a smell now and can't draw it, so it draws the look.

image.prompt: a small booklet in a wire rack, and a small dog sitting in a laundromat's doorway having been sent there by a look, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'I held the can.' The dog, banished by a look.
